_comment: Transcribed from the Info.jpg sheets in ~/Downloads/Paintings, one entry per folder. Dimensions are as written on the sheet, in centimetres. Prices are euros as digits. `folder` is the source directory and `images` the photographs in it, first one primary. All 17 sheets transcribed.

paintings.title: After Monet
paintings.description:
Claude Monet's Water Lilies have always inspired me not only for their beauty, but for their unique way of observing nature. In these paintings, the true subject is not the landscape itself, but the interplay of light, reflections on the water, and the ever-changing quality of a single moment.

This painting was born from a desire to preserve a similar sense of contemplation. I was interested not so much in the flowers themselves as in the space between them—the water, the air, the light, and the silence that bring the composition together.

To me, this work is about nature's quiet ability to slow time and remind us that its most peaceful moments are often the most meaningful.

paintings.title: Anatomy of Solitude
paintings.description:
The house in this work exists as an architectural form, yet it has lost its essential function — to provide a sense of inner refuge and stability. Suspended above the ground, it becomes a metaphor for a state in which familiar points of reference no longer sustain the individual.

The composition is built upon the tension between the openness of the horizon and the invisible boundaries of the interior. Although no physical barriers are present, movement remains impossible. Here, solitude emerges not from the absence of others, but from the inability to experience a sense of belonging — to a place, to a space, or to oneself.

The keyhole functions as a symbol of potential access, yet the key cannot be found in the visible world. The only way to unlock this threshold lies within the individual.

The empty pedestal preserves a place for what cannot be represented: inner grounding, the feeling of home, or the state in which a space once again becomes inhabitable.

This work explores the moment when silence ceases to be a form of peace and instead becomes a condition of inner isolation.

paintings.title: Composure
paintings.description:
I have always been drawn to the portraits of the Old Masters, where the focus is not on narrative, but on the person themselves. With only a few carefully chosen details, these paintings reveal not simply an appearance, but a state of being.

In this work, I wanted to preserve a sense of quietness and inner composure. Light gently reveals the face, allowing everything else to recede into shadow. The earrings become the only expressive accent - a contemporary detail that connects the tradition of classical portraiture with the present day.

I am drawn to the idea that true beauty is born not from the desire to impress, but from the ability to simply be oneself.

paintings.title: Endless Distance
paintings.description:
The house in this work exists as a symbol of home, yet its interior is deprived of any sense of completion. Beyond each window lies another interior, which in turn leads to yet another, creating an endless perspective with no possibility of ever reaching its end.

Loneliness is presented here not as isolation, but as a continuous movement away from what should provide a sense of closeness and security. The repetition of identical spaces transforms the house into a metaphor for an inner state in which the search for stability is endlessly deferred, leaving the individual in perpetual motion, unable to return.

paintings.title: Foundation
paintings.description:
I have always been fascinated by the way classical art continues to live not only in museums, but also in artists' studios. The same plaster casts, drapery, and fragments of classical architecture have remained part of the creative process for generations, preserving a connection between the past and the present.

This painting was born from a desire to depict not the objects themselves, but a space filled with memory. Each element reflects the long journey of studying form, light, and composition.

To me, this work is about an ongoing dialogue with artistic tradition - one that continues to evolve with every new generation of artists.

paintings.title: Gentleness
paintings.description:
This work grew from a desire to preserve a moment that would otherwise go unnoticed. We tend to search for meaning in extraordinary events, forgetting that life is made up of countless small gestures repeated every day.

I was interested not in painting a portrait of an animal, but in capturing a state of being - gentle, unhurried, and filled with inner calm. This painting reflects that rare kind of happiness that comes not from remarkable experiences, but from the feeling that, in this moment, nothing needs to be different.

It is a reminder that sometimes the greatest happiness lies simply in being where you feel safe.

paintings.title: Inner Weather
paintings.description:
In this work, the cloud ceases to be an element of the landscape and enters the interior. It becomes a metaphor for an inner state that gradually occupies the space, leaving it physically unchanged while completely transforming the way it is perceived.

The work explores loneliness not as the absence of other people, but as a particular way of existing within one's own inner world. Thoughts, memories, and emotions gradually fill the room, dissolving the boundary between the external and the internal. What appears weightless acquires a tangible presence, turning the room into a reflection of a state in which a person is left alone with themselves.

paintings.title: Koningswijk
paintings.description:
After my trip to Brussels, the memory of the city's main cathedral stayed with me. I found myself there completely alone, and it was this solitude that allowed me to truly experience the scale of the space. The architecture ceased to be merely a historical monument and became an emotional experience - one of silence, light, and quiet awe.

After returning home, I found inspiration in Dutch interior painting, where space itself becomes the central subject. Rather than documenting the cathedral, this painting is an attempt to preserve the sense of wonder and inner stillness I experienced in that moment.

paintings.title: Passage
paintings.description:
Architecture has always fascinated me not only through its form, but through its ability to create an emotional space. Some interiors possess a remarkable quality - they seem to invite us to slow down, listen to the silence, and spend a quiet moment alone with ourselves.

After discovering Dutch interior painting, I became particularly fascinated by the way artists transformed architecture into the true subject of their work. Their paintings were not so much about buildings as they were about light, air, and the very experience of space. While creating this painting, I wanted to continue that dialogue, preserving not the precision of architectural detail, but the inner sense of calm and contemplation that such places evoke.

paintings.title: Reflections
paintings.description:
I have always been fascinated by the way Claude Monet transformed familiar landscapes into studies of light, water, and time. His water lilies were never merely depictions of nature, but an attempt to capture the fleeting atmosphere of a passing moment.

While creating this painting, I was not interested in recreating that image, but in continuing the conversation about contemplation. Here, the water becomes a space where reflections, leaves, and blossoms exist in constant dialogue with light, allowing the focus to shift from the subject itself to a quiet sense of stillness.

To me, this painting is about a kind of beauty that does not reveal itself immediately. It asks for time, silence, and a willingness to look closely.

paintings.title: Ritual
paintings.description:
Dutch still lifes taught me to see the poetry in ordinary things. Nothing in these paintings was accidental - every object became part of a story told through light, form, and texture.

This work is my dialogue with that tradition. I wanted familiar objects to become more than everyday items, transforming instead into a quiet space where even an ordinary cup of coffee becomes a reason to pause for a moment.

I am drawn to the idea that beauty rarely asks for anything extraordinary. More often, it is already around us - we simply have to learn to notice it.

paintings.title: Solitude
paintings.description: This work explores the beauty of silence and contemplation. The swan becomes more than the depiction of a bird - it emerges as a symbol of inner peace, dignity, and fragility. The surrounding darkness enhances the sense of solitude, which is not presented as absence or isolation, but as an opportunity to be alone with oneself. Soft light gliding across the white plumage emphasizes the contrast between outward stillness and the richness of one's inner world.

paintings.title: Still Bloom
paintings.description:
After discovering Dutch painting, I became particularly fascinated by the way its artists approached the ordinary. In their floral still lifes, the subject itself was never the focus; instead, it was a careful observation of light, form, and the ever-changing nature of the natural world.

With this painting, I wanted to continue that dialogue. A single flower, placed against a dark background, invites the viewer to focus on what matters most - its fragility, graceful form, and the subtle shifts of color.

To me, this painting is about a kind of beauty that reveals itself only when we are willing to slow down and look more closely.

paintings.title: The Fragility of Being
paintings.description:
Inspired by the timeless elegance of Dutch floral masters and the dramatic lighting of the Baroque era, this piece explores the delicate balance between life and the void. I wanted to capture peonies not just as flowers, but as luminous entities emerging from the deep silence of a dark background.

I hope viewers feel a sense of quiet contemplation and reverence for the fleeting moments of beauty. The contrast of soft, tactile petals against the absolute darkness is meant to evoke a feeling of "memento vivere" — a reminder to live and appreciate the peak of bloom before it fades.

paintings.title: Transparency
paintings.description:
This work is about a state of ultimate sincerity. It is about a person who builds no walls, but instead allows the light to pass right through them.

The thin fabric here does not hide the face; it becomes a conduit between the outer world and the inner self. It is an exploration of the boundary between presence and disappearance, where fragility becomes one's greatest strength. When we stop resisting and allow the world to see our true selves, we begin to radiate light from within.

paintings.title: True Form
paintings.description:
I have always been drawn to a femininity that is free from the need to be perfect.

This work is not about the display of the body. It is about the memory of movement, the touch of fabric against the skin, and the traces of a day that has passed. I was captivated by the beauty of the moment when the outward form gradually dissolves, giving way to an inner sense of self.

To me, it is within this inner freedom that a woman's true beauty is born.

paintings.title: Without Permission
paintings.description:
This portrait is built on contradictions. The crisp white collar evokes discipline and refinement, while a single cigarette quietly disrupts that impression. I was interested in how one small detail can completely reshape the viewer's perception of a person.

We rarely see people as they truly are. Instead, we see them through our own expectations, prejudices, and cultural assumptions. Perhaps freedom begins at the moment we stop trying to conform to those expectations.

There is no provocation in her gaze, no desire to please or to be understood. Instead, it conveys quiet confidence, inner independence, and a sensuality that does not seek attention. This painting is not about a woman holding a cigarette. It is about the freedom to be oneself, regardless of the story others choose to invent.
